summary: Caveman publishes three results with a runnable harness and committed data: a 10-prompt, single-run output snapshot on claude-opus-5-5 in which, on top of an 'Answer concisely.' control, `/caveman` cuts output a further 3% at the median and `/ultracave` 35%; the caveman-compress fixtures (6,198 → 4,138 tokens across five memory files); and a browser-snapshot benchmark (121 vs 15,704 tokens on a 200-row table, while on a small form caveman's full result is 2.34x larger than Playwright's). The headline input-token result (885,793 → 591,673 tokens, 33.2%, 18 of 18 answers right, with the HTML case 9.9% worse) and the Auto result (43.7% vs 44.3% resolved at 0.46x the cost, an interim run on 85 of 169 tasks) are committed as written reports: docs/WRAP-BENCHMARK.md states the first cannot be independently reproduced from this checkout, and docs/AUTO-BENCHMARK.md states the raw trajectories are not in the repository. The 63.6% (Elastic), 1.4 to 2.4x cost cut (Adobe Research) and p = 0.82 (JetBrains) figures are third-party results, and docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md lists output reduction against default verbose replies as 'Not published' and states that no quality claim is published because no reviewed fidelity snapshot is committed.
